name: Lark (Larksuite)
verdict: Custom apps work only inside the creating tenant and need a tenant admin to approve each release, so reaching other companies likely needs a store app with Lark review. Lark and Feishu are separate platforms; low confidence.
needGuide: Yes — decide Lark or Feishu per customer region first, then plan for store-app review.

auth.detail: Likely: custom (self-built) apps use app_id/app_secret to mint tenant_access_token for their own tenant; store (marketplace/ISV) apps are installed across tenants and get tenant tokens via app_ticket; user-level access uses an authorization-code flow returning user_access_token. Not verified from docs this session (site is JS-rendered).

effort.timeToProduction: unknown (likely several weeks for store listing review)

approval.gate: Custom apps are limited to the creating tenant and need a tenant admin to approve each release. Serving other companies likely requires a store/ISV app with Lark review and directory listing. Lark (open.larksuite.com) and Feishu (open.feishu.cn) are separate platforms with separate tenants: an app must be registered on the one the customer uses.

scopes.why: Granular per-API scopes; sensitive scopes need tenant admin approval at release, and store review likely scrutinizes them.
scopes.summary: Granular permission scopes per API (messages, contacts, docs). Sensitive scopes need tenant admin approval at release; store-app review likely scrutinizes scopes (unverified).

cost: Free to build (likely); store listing terms unverified
prerequisites: Account and owner: Developer needs a Lark account in a tenant where they can create apps (developer permission may be restricted by the tenant admin).
Where you register: Lark Developer Console → Create custom app (or create a store app) → Credentials & Basic Info → Permissions & Scopes → Version Management & Release
Cost: Free to build (likely); store listing terms unverified

registerAt.path: Lark Developer Console → Create custom app (or create a store app) → Credentials & Basic Info → Permissions & Scopes → Version Management & Release

steps.do: Decide Lark vs Feishu domain per customer region (open.larksuite.com vs open.feishu.cn)
Create an app in the Developer Console and capture app_id/app_secret
Select permission scopes and enable bot/web features as needed
Implement tenant_access_token minting and, for user actions, the OAuth code flow to obtain user_access_token
Create a version and submit for release; internal tenant admin approves in the Admin Console
For external customers, apply for store (ISV) app listing and complete Lark review
Draft app description, privacy policy and scope justifications for review

roles.team: Developer needs a Lark account in a tenant where they can create apps (developer permission may be restricted by the tenant admin).
roles.console: App collaborators can be added in the Developer Console (likely, under app Collaborators); not verified.
roles.customer: Tenant admin must approve a custom app release and any admin-only scopes in the Lark Admin Console; admins can restrict availability scope.

testing: Create a free Lark tenant and a custom app there; release it internally with your own admin.
Test store-app flows only after Lark grants a test listing (unverified).

blockers.problem: Custom apps cannot be installed in other tenants
blockers.fix: Use a store app for multi-company use.

blockers.problem: Lark vs Feishu tenants do not interoperate

blockers.fix: Customer admin must approve scopes in the Admin Console or calls return permission errors.
Use official SDKs and API explorer to confirm flows.

automation.agentCan: Write token-minting and OAuth code, wire event subscriptions, draft listing copy and scope justifications, run test calls.
automation.humanMust: Create the app and complete tenant admin approvals; submit the store listing; any business verification Lark requires.

uncertain: Both Lark doc fetches returned only page metadata, so everything here is from background knowledge, not confirmed 2026 docs.
Store-app review process, timelines, fees and whether non-listed apps can be installed cross-tenant are unconfirmed.
